name: Rented-compute shard fan-out with mandatory PER-SHARD launch verification
description: Blueprint 43 of 96 (BP-IMP-06). Runs many agent work units on rented job clusters when the LOCAL RAM ceiling - not the model - is the binding constraint. The distinctive mechanism is that launch is verified PER SHARD: the workspace is shared production, so a workspace-wide run count cannot distinguish this run's shards from anyone else's, and a shard chain has already silently never launched behind exactly that signal. Two further measured constraints are encoded as gates rather than prose: a submitted job carries NO job-level timeout unless one is set explicitly, and artifacts=N/N is not doneness without a content postcondition.

units.description: Work units to shard. Below a few dozen, local is cheaper and this blueprint is contraindicated.

cluster_spec.description: Cluster shape, sized against the unit count in S0 rather than guessed

artifact_sink.description: Where per-shard results land so the LOCAL session can read them after the remote run ends

job_timeout_seconds.description: MANDATORY explicit value: a submitted job carries no job-level timeout by default, so an unset timeout is an unbounded spend

compute_credential.description: Reference name only. Expiry of this credential has silently broken runs before, so S0 authenticates it rather than assuming it.

route_if_gpu_shaped.description: S0b: a GPU-shaped workload is not an agent-shaped workload and belongs on different compute

capacity-planner.description: Sizes the cluster against the measured unit count and authenticates the credential before anything is submitted

shard-submitter.description: Submits the shard chain with an EXPLICIT per-job timeout and records the run id of each submission

launch-verifier.description: Confirms THIS shard launched, by its own run id and its own postcondition - never by a workspace-wide count

cost-reporter.description: Reports metered spend and separates it from wall-clock confounds

owner.description: Decides whether rented compute is still in scope for this estate at all

routes.reason: the verification step is the one this blueprint exists for; it does not get the cheap route

stages.title: S0 SIZE the cluster against the unit count and AUTHENTICATE the credential

work_unit.title: Size rented compute against the measured unit count and prove the credential still authenticates before any submission
work_unit.question_or_target: Compute the shard count and cluster shape from the actual unit list (not a remembered shape), confirm the compute credential still authenticates with a whoami-class call, and decide whether the workload is agent-shaped (stay) or GPU-shaped (route elsewhere). Emit the shard manifest that every later stage keys on.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: mis-sizing is paid for in metered spend; this is not a cheap-route step

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the whoami-class response proving the credential authenticates (identity only, never the credential value) plus the arithmetic from unit count to shard count to worker count, re-derivable from the manifest alone
tests_required: an expired credential must FAIL this stage rather than surface later as an empty run
a unit list of 2 must produce a smaller cluster than a unit list of 600 - a sizing function that returns the same shape for both is not reading its input
both-states control: with route_if_gpu_shaped=modal a GPU-shaped workload must route AWAY, and an agent-shaped one must stay
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: an independent reviewer who re-derives the shard count from the unit list and re-runs the identity call, without reading the planner's rationale
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BLD-0057 emitted only when shard-manifest.json exists, parses, names every shard with its unit set, and records an authenticated identity plus an explicit job timeout; otherwise FAILED:BLD-0057 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot; a second authentication failure is a credential-lifecycle matter for the owner - never re-issue or rotate it here

stages.title: No submission against an unauthenticated credential
S1 SUBMIT the shard chain with an EXPLICIT per-job timeout
An unset job-level timeout is an unbounded spend, not a default
S2 VERIFY LAUNCH PER SHARD by its own run id - never by a workspace-wide count

body.title: This run id, this state transition, this shard - a missing shard is NAMED

stages.title: Every submitted shard must be individually proven to have launched
Poll until every shard is terminal by ITS OWN postcondition

body.title: One bounded polling pass over the outstanding shards

stages.title: artifacts=N/N is a count, not a content postcondition
S3 COLLECT per-shard results into the local-readable sink
S4 REPORT metered spend, with timing confounds separated out
OWNER-DECISION: is rented compute still in scope for this estate, or is local/Modal the standing answer?
stages.prompt: Measured spend, wall-clock, and per-shard verification results are attached. Keep this substrate, route future fan-outs to another provider, or retire remote fan-out for this estate?

impact.blast_radius: metered spend on the owner's cloud account plus job runs in a SHARED production workspace; terminating the jobs stops the spend but the runs remain in the shared history

worked_example.scenario: 600 units sharded into 24 chains on a shared production workspace.
worked_example.the_recorded_failure: chain 17 was submitted but never launched. The only progress signal in use was a workspace-wide run count, which was healthy because OTHER tenants' runs filled it. 25 units silently produced nothing and the run was reported complete
worked_example.with_this_blueprint: verify-each-launch keys on chain 17's OWN run id; the state never leaves PENDING; on_item_failure=abort stops the fan-out and launch-gate fails on shards_launch_verified < shards_submitted. The missing shard is NAMED, not averaged away
worked_example.timeout_case: chain 9's job was submitted with no job-level timeout and ran for 11 hours against a hung unit. timeout-gate now refuses the submission unless job_timeout_seconds is explicitly set
worked_example.doneness_case: chain 3 reports artifacts=25/25 but eight artifacts are 0-byte. doneness-gate fails on shards_with_content_postcondition < shards_submitted - a count is not a postcondition
worked_example.credential_case: the compute credential had expired between runs. size-and-authenticate fails FIRST with an identity call, so the failure is one clear stage rather than 24 empty shards. The credential is reported, never rotated here

x_extensions.distinctive_mechanism: per-shard launch verification keyed on each shard's own run id, on a substrate where the global count is meaningless, plus an explicit-timeout gate and a content-postcondition gate over the artifact count
contraindications: NOT for small fan-outs - local is cheaper and has better observability
NOT where the work needs the local filesystem
NOT when cost visibility is unavailable - metered spend without a cost report is an open-ended commitment
x_extensions.not_a_duplicate_because: BP-IMP-05 targets many REPOSITORIES on their own CI with a propose-only constraint; this targets many WORK UNITS on rented compute, and its defining gate is per-shard launch verification on a shared-tenant substrate.
